lq.ANSWER:
1. Definition and Principles of Distributed Computing (5 marks)

Distributed computing is a model where tasks are split across multiple machines (nodes) that communicate over a network.
Core principles:

  • Resource sharing (CPU, storage)

  • Scalability (horizontal scaling)

  • Fault tolerance (if one node fails, others continue)

  • Transparency in communication and data access

2. Shared vs Distributed Memory Comparison (6 marks)

Feature Shared Memory Distributed Memory
Communication Via shared variables Via message passing
Scalability Limited (single system) High (multi-node clusters)
Fault Tolerance Low High
Use Case Example Real-time graphics rendering Big data processing (Hadoop, Spark)

3. Recommendation and Justification (4 marks)

Recommendation: Distributed memory architecture
Justification:

  • E-commerce analytics requires scalable and fault-tolerant systems.

  • Distributed systems can handle large datasets across nodes, ensuring high performance even with growing users and data.
lq.QUESTION_DESC:
You are part of a data engineering team handling a large-scale analytics system for an e-commerce platform. As daily transactions grow, your team is evaluating whether to use shared memory or distributed computing to scale the system efficiently. The goal is to process huge volumes of data across multiple nodes with high availability and speed.

Task:

  1. Define distributed computing and explain its core principles. (5 marks)

  2. Compare shared memory and distributed memory models with examples of suitable real-world use cases. (6 marks)

  3. Recommend which architecture (shared or distributed) is more suitable for the e-commerce analytics system, and justify your choice in terms of scalability and fault tolerance. (4 marks)
